title: He did not fall in one night.
paragraphs:
He did not fall in one night.
He drifted in silence.
Solomon did not wake up one morning and decide, “I will turn from God.”

It was slower than that.
Softer than that.
More dangerous than that.
“For when Solomon was old, his wives turned away his heart after other gods, and his heart was not wholly true to the LORD his God…” (1 Kings 11:4)
That is the terror of spiritual drift.

Not always rebellion with a shout.
Sometimes it is compromise with a whisper.
A heart once burning for God can grow crowded.
Not empty.
Crowded.

Solomon still had wisdom.
Still had power.
Still had wealth.
But somewhere along the way, he lost wholeness.
And that is what destroys many people in secret.

Not the sudden scandal.
The silent division.
A little affection here.
A little compromise there.
A slow tolerance for what once grieved you.
A prayer life that cools without alarm.
A conscience that adjusts to what it should confront.

The tragedy of Solomon is not just that he loved foreign women more than he loved wisdom.
It is that a divided heart can sit near sacred things and still drift far from God.

You can know worship songs and still wander.
You can speak truth and still be starving inside.
You can carry influence and still be losing intimacy with the Lord.

Brother, sister—Jesus did not come merely to improve a drifting heart.
He came to rescue it.

Where Solomon’s heart became divided, Christ remained fully devoted to the Father.
Where kings failed, Jesus obeyed.
Where our loves get scattered, Christ gathers us back through His cross.
His blood is strong enough to cleanse compromise.
His grace is strong enough to call prodigals home.
His Spirit is strong enough to make your heart whole again.
So do not ignore the drift.

Bring it into the light.
Repent early.
Return quickly.
Cry out honestly.
Because the God who exposes the wandering heart is also the Savior who restores it.
No matter how far your affections have slipped, Jesus still receives the one who comes broken and true.
Come back while your heart can still feel His voice.
